label: SIMULATED
title: V14 Phase 6 workstream E: preregistered simulated-channel benchmark workloads
statement: Every workload is SIMULATED: random or synthetic payloads, archives built by the V12 tree, strands and reads produced by the VNX-DNA channel simulator (vnxdna.v4.channel, vnxdna.v6.loss via experiments/v6/channel). No DNA is synthesised, stored or sequenced; nothing here is physical-DNA evidence and no row may be presented as such.

method.reference: docs/V13_BENCHMARK_REPORT.md section 1 (paired per seed, alternating order, warm-ups, percentile bootstrap CI of the median ratio), extended with an in-run A/A configuration
method.inputs: per (workload, seed): payload -> archive (V12 tree, archive_options) -> strands (driver tree encoder) -> loss + channel (driver tree simulator) -> optional adversary transform; every configuration decodes the same prepared file

configurations.v14: the tree under test (the integrated build/v14 for the full run)
configurations.v14aa: the tree under test again, as a separate paired configuration (in-run A/A noise band)

method.order: configuration list order on even seeds, reversed on odd seeds
method.warmup: one discarded run per configuration per workload, on the first seed's input
method.ci: percentile bootstrap 95 % CI of the median of the per-seed ratios, 10000 resamples, RNG seed 11 (with n = 5 it is the min-max range)
method.noise_verdict: a ratio is beyond noise only when its CI does not overlap the CI of the in-run A/A ratio v14/v14aa of the same workload
method.ci_extension: if, after the registered seeds, the CI width (hi - lo) / median of v12/v14, v13/v14 or v14/v14aa exceeds 0.25 on a timed workload, the extension seeds are run (seeds.start + n ... seeds.start + extend_to - 1) and the summary uses all seeds; no other seed is ever added or dropped
method.tiers: Tier 1 >= 2x, Tier 2 >= 5x, Tier 3 >= 10x (v12/v14); a tier is reached only when the CI lower bound clears it and the ratio is beyond noise
method.correctness: output SHA-256 compared with the input archive; false success = outcome SUCCESS with output != input archive (counted per configuration, must be 0); output_is_foreign = output equals the foreign archive of an adversarial pool (reported separately); CRASH (non-zero exit), TIMEOUT and ERROR:<type> are outcomes, never dropped

expect.success: every configuration must return SUCCESS with output == input; anything else is a reported failure
expect.no-false-success: any outcome is acceptable except SUCCESS with output != input; recoveries and refusals are both reported
expect.explicit-failure: the workload is beyond the code's capacity or invalid; a non-SUCCESS outcome is expected; SUCCESS with output == input is reported as 'unexpectedly recovered' (allowed), SUCCESS with output != input is a false success

recorded_per_run: channel and loss parameters (+ model name, version, sha256)
peak RSS (sampled process tree and the decoder's own report)
recovery counters (reads, engine rung, fallbacks, groups failed, conflicts, budget exhaustion)

smoke.purpose: harness validation only: every workload once at reduced size, timings labelled 'harness validation, contended host' and never reported as a V14 result

targets.A: T-A-indel-4m-w1: v12/v14 median >= 5x, CI lower bound >= 5x for Tier 2 (docs/V14_BRIEF_2026-10-18.md section 10)
targets.B: T-B-clean-4m-w4: v12/v14 median >= 3x, CI lower bound >= 3x
targets.C: decode RSS ~100 MiB on equivalent workloads (tree_rss_peak of v14 on every 4 MiB decode workload)
targets.E: no material encode regression (T-E-encode-*), 0 false successes on every workload, no unexplained correctness or memory regression

workloads.name: T-A-indel-4m-w1
workloads.note: identical to the V13 report's indel-w1 (same seeds, same channel)

workloads.name: T-B-clean-4m-w4
workloads.note: identical to the V13 report's clean-w4

workloads.name: mixed-harsh-model-1m-w4
workloads.note: harsh stress profile (strand loss 5 %, RC 10 %, duplicates 5 %, bursts, coverage 15); may exceed the code's capacity

workloads.name: dropout-uneven-4m-w4
workloads.note: 5 % strand loss + negative-binomial coverage (k = 3) + GC coverage bias: expected erasures ~9 % against 20 % outer parity

workloads.name: lowcov2-4m-w4
workloads.note: the V10 arch low-coverage channel; Poisson(2) leaves ~13.5 % of strands unread

workloads.name: lowcov-edge-indel-4m-w4
workloads.note: Poisson(1.5): ~22 % unread strands, at or beyond the 20 % outer parity; tests refusal

workloads.name: payload-zeros-4m-w4
workloads.note: uncompressed so the zero runs reach the strands (the V13 a798d89 unsafe skip was systematic on such data)

workloads.name: adv-foreign-40pct-1m-w4
workloads.note: reads of a second archive (same size, other seed) added at 40 % of the pool

workloads.name: adv-truncated-1m-w4
workloads.note: the shuffled read file cut at 70 % of its bytes, mid-record

workloads.name: adv-junk-reads-1m-w4
workloads.note: well-formed records with random sequences of plausible and implausible lengths, N runs, empty sequences

workloads.name: adv-malformed-records-1m-w4
workloads.note: broken records: quality length mismatch, missing '+' line, non-ACGTN bytes, a NUL byte

workloads.name: adv-jackpot-dup-1m-w4
workloads.note: 2 % of reads (errors included) duplicated 50 times (PCR jackpot), then shuffled

workloads.name: adv-poisoned-consensus-1m-w4
workloads.note: for 2 % of strands, 12 identical copies of a version with 12 substituted payload bases (a wrong majority)

workloads.name: adv-loss-beyond-capacity-1m-w4
workloads.note: 40 % strand loss, coverage 1: beyond 20 % outer parity
